evidence.testName: a registry cell with exactly one persisted row shows insufficient history, never a sparkline

results.note: The test builds a single point directly and renders <Sparkline>. It asserts there is no svg or polyline, checks the 'Not enough history yet (1 point since 28 Sep 2026)' text, and checks the dateTime attribute. The test gate ran npm --prefix web test and exited 0. One caveat: the test renders the component in isolation and does not go through the history_read path, but the scenario is built deterministically as the criterion requires.

The test is marked @pytest.mark.integration, and pyproject.toml:33 sets addopts '-m not integration', so the gate never ran it. The evidence directory holds only a markdown file with no recorded run or output, so nothing shows the seam check has ever passed. The design is also weak. The 'fresh live call' (fetch_btc_funding_rate_history, limit=2) hits the same OKX funding-rate-history endpoint that the backfill uses, with only limit/before changed. The story title asks for a cross-vendor check, which this is not. The test also works in an empty temporary schema that has no live rows, so it never actually checks a live/backfill overlap in the data.

The test applies all migrations to an isolated schema and persists a live row. It then calls the real run_backfill orchestrator, which persists a row with a higher id. It asserts that board_read and datapoints_read return only the live row, and that the backfill row exists with origin='backfill'. The vendor fetch is replaced with a stub recipe, but the backfill and persistence path is real. The test skips if it cannot connect to the database. .env.local exists, so it very likely ran under the gate, which exited 0.
This is a human criterion. A person must look at the live board and compare it against the vendor's own data.

note: The sparse-history test and the board_read splice test are real tests with meaningful assertions. The key seam check (C2) is excluded from the gate by the 'not integration' addopts and has no run evidence, and it re-queries the same OKX endpoint the backfill used instead of making a cross-vendor or independent check. The diff also includes unrelated SESSION.md and events.ndjson bookkeeping churn.
